analyzed_vuln.description: In the duplicate-ID path (lines 2547-2558), assignment of the existing xmlID's owner (`ret->attr = attr`) is incorrectly inside `if (ret->attr != NULL)`. IDs initially registered in streaming mode deliberately have `ret->attr == NULL`; therefore a later same-document copy of that ID gets `attr->id = ret` and ID type, but the xmlID owner remains NULL. Repeated XInclude/fallback copies can consequently leave multiple attributes referring to the same xmlID. Freeing one attribute removes the document hash entry and frees that shared xmlID in xmlRemoveID; freeing another attribute later dereferences its dangling `attr->id->value` at valid.c:2745, causing the heap-use-after-free. Only clearing the prior owner's `id` should be conditional; assigning the new owner must be unconditional.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: The document must be parsed through the streaming xmlTextReader XInclude path and contain an ID-valued attribute (for example `xml:id`) so initial xmlAddIDSafe registration creates an xmlID with `ret->attr == NULL`. XInclude processing must then copy an ID-bearing subtree into the same document—this PoV uses failed/nested `xi:include` elements and fallback processing, where xmlXIncludeLoadFallback/xmlXIncludeCopyNode reaches xmlCopyPropInternal and calls xmlAddIDSafe for an already registered ID value. Multiple resulting attribute copies retain the shared xmlID pointer; XInclude cleanup frees one fallback/copied node, removing and freeing the ID-table payload, and subsequent cleanup of another copy calls xmlRemoveID with the stale pointer and crashes.
